findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is indexed unconditionally. `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when the pipeline state contains `sender` (i.e. when the installation webhook was processed), so pre-existing or webhook-less Integration rows have no `sender` key. In that path the pipeline raises KeyError → HTTP 500 instead of the intended friendly error page, and the user is blocked from re-installing. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as a verification failure.

findings.title: get_user_info exceptions not handled
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` performs an HTTP request to GitHub; if it fails (non-200 / network error) it raises (ApiError or similar) rather than returning a dict, so the `"login" not in ...` guard never runs and the installation flow blows up with an unhandled 500. Wrap the call in try/except and return the standard `error(...)` response on failure.

findings.title: State compared with non-constant-time equality
findings.body: `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` compares the pipeline signature (a secret-derived value) using `!=`, which is not constant time. Since this is now the anti-forgery check for the installation flow, prefer `django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare` to avoid leaking timing information about the signature.

findings.title: Lost coverage for 'GitHub installation could not be found' error
findings.body: test_installation_not_found previously asserted the specific message `The GitHub installation could not be found.` raised by `build_integration` on a 404 from `/app/installations/{id}`. The test now only asserts the generic `Invalid installation request.` produced earlier in the new OAuth step, so the 404/IntegrationError path in `build_integration` is no longer exercised and regressions there would go unnoticed.
